Generate realisations of a fitted curve over a predictor grid

Source: R/toxval-predict.R
toxval_predict.Rd

Evaluates a fitted concentration-response model over a grid of predictor values, once per realisation of the fit. The result can be passed to ecx() and nsec() in place of the fitted model.

Usage

toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

# Default S3 method
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'brmsfit'
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL,
  asymptote = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'drc'
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL,
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bayesnecfit'
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bayesmanecfit'
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bnecfit'
toxval_predict(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A model fitted with brms, drc or bayesnec.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods, such as n_boot and seed for a drc fit, or asymptote for a brmsfit.

x_var

A string naming the predictor variable in object, or NULL where the class of object records which of its variables is the predictor. Each method states whether it accepts NULL.

group_var

A string naming the grouping variable in object, or NULL for a single curve.

resolution

A whole number giving the number of predictor values to evaluate the curve at. Larger values estimate a metric more precisely.

x_range

A numeric vector of length 2 giving the range of predictor values to evaluate over, or NULL to use the range in the model data. The first value must equal the control concentration.

x_control

A number, the control concentration, at which the control response is predicted and the grid starts, or NULL for the lowest predictor value in the data. A value outside the range of the data warns.

asymptote

The lower and upper asymptotes of a brmsfit, for type = "relative", as a vector named decreasing, increasing or both. Each is the name of a non-linear parameter, such as c(decreasing = "bot", increasing = "top"), or a number on the response scale.

n_boot

A whole number giving the number of parametric bootstrap replicates to draw.

seed

A whole number used to seed the bootstrap draw, or NULL to use the current random number state.

Value

A toxval_pred object.

Details

Realisations are posterior draws for a Bayesian fit and parametric bootstrap replicates for a frequentist one. A bootstrap replicate is drawn from a multivariate normal with the coefficients as its mean and their covariance.

Supply group_var to get one curve per level rather than a single curve. The curves follow the order of the levels of a factor, and otherwise their sorted order. Each method states what group_var must name.

The grid starts at the control concentration, where the control response is predicted, and every reference, ECx and NSEC is measured from that response. By default the control concentration is the lowest predictor value in the data. Use x_control to name another, such as 0 for a predictor measured as the reduction from an ambient level. A value outside the range of the data warns. A grouped fit has one control concentration for every curve.

Methods (by class)

  • toxval_predict(default): Method for any class without one, which errors.

  • toxval_predict(brmsfit): Method for a brms::brmsfit. Realisations are the posterior draws, with group-level effects excluded. x_var is required. group_var must name a population-level effect; a variable that appears only in a group-level term, such as site in y ~ x + (1 | site), is an error.

    A multivariate fit gives one curve per response, named as brms names them, for example spsurvival for a column sp_survival.

    A binomial response, such as y | trials(n) ~ x, is predicted at one trial, so control and reference are proportions. The NSEC and ECx do not depend on the number of trials.

    type = "relative" needs asymptote, and is not supported for a multivariate fit.

  • toxval_predict(drc): Method for a fit from drc::drm(). Realisations are parametric bootstrap replicates, so results vary between calls unless seed is supplied. A parameter that must be positive, such as e in LL.4(), is drawn on the log scale. x_var is read from the fit if not supplied. group_var must name the column passed as curveid. The asymptotes used by type = "relative" are the lower and upper limits of the fitted function.

  • toxval_predict(bayesnecfit): Method for a single fit from bayesnec::bnec(), of class bayesnecfit, which requires bayesnec to be installed. Realisations are the posterior draws, with group-level effects excluded. x_var is read from the crf() term if not supplied. group_var must be NULL. A predictor transformed inside crf(), such as crf(log(x), ...), is reported in units of x, so xform = exp must not be supplied. A binomial or beta-binomial response is predicted at one trial, so its curve is a proportion. The asymptotes used by type = "relative" are the bot parameter, or 0 for an equation without one, and 1 for a proportion. An asymptote is NA where the family has no such bound or the link is not identity.

  • toxval_predict(bayesmanecfit): Method for a model average from bayesnec::bnec(), of class bayesmanecfit, which requires bayesnec to be installed. Each model is predicted as for a bayesnecfit. Realisations are the draws bayesnec keeps from each model in proportion to its weight, the same draws its own estimates use, and each takes its asymptotes from its own model. The random number state of the session is left unchanged.

  • toxval_predict(bnecfit): Method for any other bayesnec fit, which errors. Group fits, joint refits and hurdle pairs each hold more than one curve, over concentrations that can differ between curves, which a toxval_pred does not yet represent.

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- drc::drm(rootl ~ conc, data = drc::ryegrass, fct = drc::LL.4())
toxval_predict(fit, seed = 42)
#> <toxval_pred> drc
#>   realisations: 1000 (bootstrap)
#>   grid:         conc, 500 values from 0 to 30
#>   curves:       1 (ungrouped)
#>   threshold:    none
#>   control:      none
if (requireNamespace("bayesnec", quietly = TRUE)) {
  toxval_predict(bayesnec::manec_example)
}
#> <toxval_pred> bayesmanecfit
#>   realisations: 100 (draws)
#>   grid:         x, 500 values from 0.03234801 to 3.22052
#>   curves:       1 (ungrouped)
#>   threshold:    none
#>   control:      none
# }
